// emails/newsletter/designs/roundup.tsx: a design made from the template.

import { Button, Column, Heading, Image, Link, List, ListItem, Text, token } from "@hyper-elements/react";
import Newsletter from "./template";

export const meta = { label: "Community roundup" };

export default function Roundup() {
  return (
    <Newsletter
      subject="The best of the community this month"
      preview="A template library from our users, three talks worth your lunch break, and the next meetup"
      issue="Roundup · Spring edition"
      body={
        <Column style={{ gap: token("spacing.lg") }}>
          <Image
            src={{ src: "https://hyperelements.dev/generated/gallery/assets/images/shapes.png", width: 1600, height: 1200 }}
            alt=""
            style={{ borderRadius: token("radii.sm") }}
          />
          <Column style={{ gap: token("spacing.md") }}>
            <Heading level={1}>A shared library of 200 templates</Heading>
            <Text>
              Teams have been posting the templates they use every week. Browse them by job, copy one into your workspace, and make it yours in a minute.
            </Text>
            <Button href="https://orbit.example/community/templates">Browse the template library</Button>
          </Column>
          <Column style={{ gap: token("spacing.sm") }}>
            <Heading level={2}>Three talks worth your lunch break</Heading>
            <List>
              <ListItem>Planning a launch with a team of three</ListItem>
              <ListItem>Writing for readers who skim</ListItem>
              <ListItem>What a hundred onboarding emails taught us</ListItem>
            </List>
            <Text>
              <Link href="https://orbit.example/community/talks">Watch the talks from the last meetup</Link>
            </Text>
          </Column>
          <Column style={{ backgroundColor: token("colors.surface"), borderRadius: token("radii.sm"), padding: token("spacing.lg"), gap: token("spacing.sm") }}>
            <Heading level={3}>Meet us in person</Heading>
            <Text>The next meetup is an evening of short talks and good snacks. Seats go quickly.</Text>
            <Button href="https://orbit.example/community/meetups">Save a seat at the meetup</Button>
          </Column>
        </Column>
      }
    />
  );
}

Find what you want, faster

Tips and tricks for searching on Stack Overflow

Searching for solutions

With more than 18 million questions, it's possible that someone has already provided a solution to the problem you're facing.

 

Use the search bar at the top of the page to find what you need

Here are a few simple search tips to get you started:

•
To find a specific phrase, enter it in quotes: "local storage"
•
To search within specific tag(s), enter them in square brackets: [javascript]
•
Combine them to get even more precise results - [javascript] "local storage" searches for the phrase “local storage” in questions that have the [javascript] tag

The more information you can put in the search bar, the more likely you will be to either find the answer you need or feel confident that no one else has asked the question before.

Tips and tricks for searching on Stack Overflow

Searching for solutions

With more than 18 million questions, it's possible that someone has already provided a solution to the problem you're facing.

 

Use the search bar at the top of the page to find what you need

Here are a few simple search tips to get you started:

•
To find a specific phrase, enter it in quotes: "local storage"
•
To search within specific tag(s), enter them in square brackets: [javascript]
•
Combine them to get even more precise results - [javascript] "local storage" searches for the phrase “local storage” in questions that have the [javascript] tag

The more information you can put in the search bar, the more likely you will be to either find the answer you need or feel confident that no one else has asked the question before.

Find what you want, faster

Tips and tricks for searching on Stack Overflow

Searching for solutions

With more than 18 million questions, it's possible that someone has already provided a solution to the problem you're facing.

 

Use the search bar at the top of the page to find what you need

Here are a few simple search tips to get you started:

•
To find a specific phrase, enter it in quotes: "local storage"
•
To search within specific tag(s), enter them in square brackets: [javascript]
•
Combine them to get even more precise results - [javascript] "local storage" searches for the phrase “local storage” in questions that have the [javascript] tag

The more information you can put in the search bar, the more likely you will be to either find the answer you need or feel confident that no one else has asked the question before.

Find what you want, faster

Tips and tricks for searching on Stack Overflow

Searching for solutions

With more than 18 million questions, it's possible that someone has already provided a solution to the problem you're facing.

 

Use the search bar at the top of the page to find what you need

Here are a few simple search tips to get you started:

•
To find a specific phrase, enter it in quotes: "local storage"
•
To search within specific tag(s), enter them in square brackets: [javascript]
•
Combine them to get even more precise results - [javascript] "local storage" searches for the phrase “local storage” in questions that have the [javascript] tag

The more information you can put in the search bar, the more likely you will be to either find the answer you need or feel confident that no one else has asked the question before.

payouts.description: The email once an account can take live payments: the logo, short paragraphs with links into the docs, one button, and the address
payouts.html:
Your bank account is verified, so your balance now pays out on your schedule͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ 
 

Your bank account is verified. From now on, your available balance is paid out to it automatically, on the schedule you choose.

You can follow each payout, and the payments it includes, from your dashboard.

View your payouts
 

Payouts are made every business day to start with. To be paid weekly or monthly instead, change your payout schedule.

Payout timing depends on your bank: most payouts arrive within two business days. You can pause payouts when you need to, or send an instant payout that arrives in minutes.

Each payout shows up on your bank statement with the description you set in your statement settings.

Questions about a payout? You can find answers and get in touch with us on our support site.

— The Stripe team

 

Stripe, 354 Oyster Point Blvd, South San Francisco, CA 94080

Thanks for submitting your account information. You're now ready to make live transactions with Stripe!

You can view your payments and a variety of other information about your account right from your dashboard.

View your Stripe Dashboard
 

If you haven't finished your integration, you might find our docs handy.

Once you're ready to start accepting payments, you'll just need to use your live API keys instead of your test API keys. Your account can simultaneously be used for both test and live requests, so you can continue testing while accepting live payments. Check out our tutorial about account basics.

Finally, we've put together a quick checklist to ensure your website conforms to card network standards.

We'll be here to help you with any step along the way. You can find answers to most questions and get in touch with us on our support site.

— The Pell & Ashby team

 

Pell & Ashby, 3 Lincoln's Court, Philadelphia

payouts.html:
Your bank account is verified, so your balance now pays out on your schedule͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ ͏‌ 
 

Your bank account is verified. From now on, your available balance is paid out to it automatically, on the schedule you choose.

You can follow each payout, and the payments it includes, from your dashboard.

View your payouts
 

Payouts are made every business day to start with. To be paid weekly or monthly instead, change your payout schedule.

Payout timing depends on your bank: most payouts arrive within two business days. You can pause payouts when you need to, or send an instant payout that arrives in minutes.

Each payout shows up on your bank statement with the description you set in your statement settings.

Questions about a payout? You can find answers and get in touch with us on our support site.

— The Pell & Ashby team

 

Pell & Ashby, 3 Lincoln's Court, Philadelphia

You can pause payouts (https://slowsignals.example/docs/payouts/pause) when you need to, or send an instant payout (https://slowsignals.example/docs/payouts/instant) that arrives in minutes.

Each payout shows up on your bank statement with the description you set in your statement settings (https://slowsignals.example/dashboard/settings/statement).

Questions about a payout? You can find answers and get in touch with us on our support site (https://slowsignals.example/support).

— The Slow Signals team

Maker Meetup

An evening of show and tell for people who build small tools, with demos, snacks and plenty of time to talk.

Join the waitlist for Maker Meetup

Oct

8

When

6:00 PM to 9:30 PM

Where

Harbor Hall

9 Quay Street

Halifax, NS B3J 1A1

Canada

And online

Join Maker Meetup online

Tickets

$15, with supper; free to watch online

Join the waitlist

What to expect

Every demo runs ten minutes, and the makers stay for the evening to answer questions at their tables.

  • Bring a laptop if you'd like to try the tools yourself.
  • The demos stream live, with questions from the chat read out on stage.

6:00 PM

Plugins that never break on update

PC

Priya Castellan

// documents/datasheet/designs/wr-4.tsx: a design made from the template.

import Datasheet from "./template";

export const meta = { label: "WR-4 six-axis motion sensor" };

const values = {
  part: "WR-4",
  name: "Motion sensor",
  revision: "A",
  date: "September",
  summary: "A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.",
  highlights: [
    { value: "±2000 °/s", label: "Gyroscope, full scale" },
    { value: "±16 g", label: "Accelerometer, full scale" },
    { value: "0.9 mA", label: "Both sensors running" },
    { value: "6.4 kHz", label: "Fastest output rate" },
  ],
  features: [
    "Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock",
    "Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C",
    "Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V",
    "I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz",
    "Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall",
    "Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes",
  ],
  applications: [
    "Drones and model aircraft",
    "Gait and posture logging",
    "Vibration monitoring",
    "Camera stabilisers",
  ],
  description: "WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.",

WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

1VINPowerSupply, 3.0 to 5.5 V. The on-board regulator makes 3.3 V.

wr-4.html:
WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

04 DESCRIPTION

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

Pin | Name | Type | Description
1 | VIN | Power | Supply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2 | GND | Ground | Ground.
3 | SCL | Input | I²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4 | SDA | I/O | I²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5 | SDO | Output | SPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6 | CS | Input | SPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7 | INT1 | Output | Interrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8 | INT2 | Output | Interrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9 | FSYNC | Input | Frame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10 | GND | Ground | Ground.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

03   Pinout

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

1VINPowerSupply, 3.0 to 5.5 V. The on-board regulator makes 3.3 V.

wr-4.title: WR-4 six-axis motion sensor, Keel
wr-4.description: An A4 hardware datasheet with a pinout, electrical limits, performance curves, I²C timing, an application schematic and a dimensioned board outline.
wr-4.html:
WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.text:
Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01 FEATURES

- Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
- Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
- Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
- I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
- Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
- Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02 APPLICATIONS

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03 PINOUT

04 DESCRIPTION

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

Pin | Name | Type | Description
1 | VIN | Power | Supply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2 | GND | Ground | Ground.
3 | SCL | Input | I²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4 | SDA | I/O | I²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5 | SDO | Output | SPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6 | CS | Input | SPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7 | INT1 | Output | Interrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8 | INT2 | Output | Interrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9 | FSYNC | Input | Frame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10 | GND | Ground | Ground.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

Symbol | Parameter | Min | Max | Unit
fSCL | Clock frequency | 0 | 1000 | kHz
tHD;STA | Hold time, START | 0.26 | – | µs
tLOW | Clock low | 0.5 | – | µs
tHIGH | Clock high | 0.26 | – | µs
tSU;DAT | Data set-up time | 50 | – | ns
tHD;DAT | Data hold time | 0 | – | µs
tSU;STO | Set-up time, STOP | 0.26 | – | µs
tBUF | Bus free, STOP to START | 0.5 | – | µs

Table 4 I²C timing, fast-mode plus.

WR-4 answers at 0x68 with SDO low and at 0x69 with SDO high. The board holds CS high, so it starts in I²C.

For SDA and SCL, use 1 kΩ pull-ups to 3.3 V. At 100 pF per line, the estimated rise time is 84.7 ns (120 ns max, UM10204).

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

wr-4.title: WR-4 six-axis motion sensor, Oyen
wr-4.description: An A4 hardware datasheet with a pinout, electrical limits, performance curves, I²C timing, an application schematic and a dimensioned board outline.
wr-4.html:
WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.text:
Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01 FEATURES

- Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
- Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
- Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
- I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
- Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
- Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02 APPLICATIONS

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03 PINOUT

Top view

[WR-4 from above at 1.5 : 1: the board, its 10 pads called out by number and name, and its mounting holes.]

Figure 1 WR-4 from above at 1.5 : 1. Each pad is drawn and called out from table 1.

04 DESCRIPTION

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

Pin | Name | Type | Description
1 | VIN | Power | Supply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2 | GND | Ground | Ground.
3 | SCL | Input | I²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4 | SDA | I/O | I²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5 | SDO | Output | SPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6 | CS | Input | SPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7 | INT1 | Output | Interrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8 | INT2 | Output | Interrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9 | FSYNC | Input | Frame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10 | GND | Ground | Ground.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-4 answers at 0x68 with SDO low and at 0x69 with SDO high. The board holds CS high, so it starts in I²C.

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

wr-4.title: WR-4 six-axis motion sensor, Pell & Ashby
wr-4.description: An A4 hardware datasheet with a pinout, electrical limits, performance curves, I²C timing, an application schematic and a dimensioned board outline.
wr-4.html:
WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-4 answers at 0x68 with SDO low and at 0x69 with SDO high. The board holds CS high, so it starts in I²C.

wr-4.text:
Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01 FEATURES

- Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
- Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
- Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
- I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
- Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
- Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02 APPLICATIONS

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03 PINOUT

04 DESCRIPTION

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

Pin | Name | Type | Description
1 | VIN | Power | Supply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2 | GND | Ground | Ground.
3 | SCL | Input | I²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4 | SDA | I/O | I²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5 | SDO | Output | SPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6 | CS | Input | SPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7 | INT1 | Output | Interrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8 | INT2 | Output | Interrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9 | FSYNC | Input | Frame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10 | GND | Ground | Ground.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-4 answers at 0x68 with SDO low and at 0x69 with SDO high. The board holds CS high, so it starts in I²C.

For SDA and SCL, use 1 kΩ pull-ups to 3.3 V. At 100 pF per line, the estimated rise time is 84.7 ns (120 ns max, UM10204).

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

03   Pinout

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 3.0 to 5.5 V. The on-board regulator makes 3.3 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock. Pull up to 3.3 V on the host.
4SDAI/OI²C data, open drain. Pull up to 3.3 V on the host.
5INTOutputData ready, active low, open drain.
6ADDRInputI²C address: low for 0x76, high for 0x77. Pulled low on the board.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.title: WR-4 six-axis motion sensor, Pith
wr-4.description: An A4 hardware datasheet with a pinout, electrical limits, performance curves, I²C timing, an application schematic and a dimensioned board outline.
wr-4.html:
WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03   Pinout

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.text:
Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01 FEATURES

- Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
- Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
- Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
- I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
- Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
- Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02 APPLICATIONS

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03 PINOUT

Top view

[WR-4 from above at 1.5 : 1: the board, its 10 pads called out by number and name, and its mounting holes.]

04 DESCRIPTION

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

Pin | Name | Type | Description
1 | VIN | Power | Supply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2 | GND | Ground | Ground.
3 | SCL | Input | I²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4 | SDA | I/O | I²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5 | SDO | Output | SPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6 | CS | Input | SPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7 | INT1 | Output | Interrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8 | INT2 | Output | Interrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9 | FSYNC | Input | Frame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10 | GND | Ground | Ground.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 3.0 to 5.5 V. The on-board regulator makes 3.3 V.

4SDAI/OI²C data, open drain. Pull up to 3.3 V on the host.
5INTOutputData ready, active low, open drain.
6ADDRInputI²C address: low for 0x76, high for 0x77. Pulled low on the board.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.title: WR-4 six-axis motion sensor, Quarry
wr-4.description: An A4 hardware datasheet with a pinout, electrical limits, performance curves, I²C timing, an application schematic and a dimensioned board outline.
wr-4.html:
WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03   Pinout

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.text:
Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01 FEATURES

- Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
- Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
- Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
- I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
- Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
- Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02 APPLICATIONS

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03 PINOUT

[WR-4 from above at 1.5 : 1: the board, its 10 pads called out by number and name, and its mounting holes.]

04 DESCRIPTION

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

Pin | Name | Type | Description
1 | VIN | Power | Supply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2 | GND | Ground | Ground.
3 | SCL | Input | I²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4 | SDA | I/O | I²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5 | SDO | Output | SPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6 | CS | Input | SPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7 | INT1 | Output | Interrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8 | INT2 | Output | Interrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9 | FSYNC | Input | Frame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10 | GND | Ground | Ground.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

WR-2 Datasheet · Rev C

Revision C · March

WR-2

Environmental sensor

Temperature, humidity, pressure and air quality on a 25 × 18 mm board, read over I²C.

±0.2 °C

Temperature, 0 to 65 °C

±2 %RH

Humidity, 20 to 80 %RH

±0.6 hPa

Pressure, 300 to 1100 hPa

3.4 µA

Asleep, between readings

01   Features

  • Temperature, humidity, pressure and VOC on one board
  • Calibrated in the factory: ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH
  • Runs from 3.0 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C up to 400 kHz, at either of two addresses
  • 3.4 µA asleep, 0.9 mA while measuring
  • Castellated pads on a 2.54 mm pitch: solder it flat or fit a header

02   Applications

Indoor air quality monitors · Ventilation and HVAC control · Weather stations · Greenhouse and cold-store loggers · Battery-powered sensor nodes

04   Description

WR-2 measures temperature, relative humidity, barometric pressure and volatile organic compounds, and reports all four over I²C. A low-dropout regulator lets it run from 3.0 to 5.5 V while its logic stays at 3.3 V, and it sleeps at 3.4 µA between readings.

1VINPowerSupply, 3.0 to 5.5 V. The on-board regulator makes 3.3 V.

4SDAI/OI²C data, open drain. Pull up to 3.3 V on the host.

6ADDRInputI²C address: low for 0x76, high for 0x77. Pulled low on the board.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.title: WR-4 six-axis motion sensor, Slow Signals
wr-4.description: An A4 hardware datasheet with a pinout, electrical limits, performance curves, I²C timing, an application schematic and a dimensioned board outline.
wr-4.html:
WR-4 Datasheet · Rev A

Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01   Features

  • Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
  • Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
  • Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
  • I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
  • Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
  • Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02   Applications

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

04   Description

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

PinNameTypeDescription
1VINPowerSupply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2GNDGroundGround.
3SCLInputI²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4SDAI/OI²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5SDOOutputSPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6CSInputSPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7INT1OutputInterrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8INT2OutputInterrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9FSYNCInputFrame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10GNDGroundGround.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.

wr-4.text:
Revision A · September

WR-4

Motion sensor

A six-axis gyroscope and accelerometer on a 30 × 22 mm board, read over I²C or SPI.

±2000 °/s

Gyroscope, full scale

±16 g

Accelerometer, full scale

0.9 mA

Both sensors running

6.4 kHz

Fastest output rate

01 FEATURES

- Three-axis gyroscope and three-axis accelerometer on one clock
- Trimmed in the factory: ±0.5 °/s and ±20 mg offsets at 25 °C
- Runs from 2.4 to 5.5 V; logic stays at 3.3 V
- I²C at up to 1 MHz, or SPI at up to 10 MHz
- Two interrupt pins: data ready, motion and free fall
- Ten castellated pads on two edges, and four M2.5 holes

02 APPLICATIONS

Drones and model aircraft · Gait and posture logging · Vibration monitoring · Camera stabilisers

03 PINOUT

04 DESCRIPTION

WR-4 measures rotation on three axes and acceleration on three more, and stamps every sample from one clock so the two line up. Read it over I²C or SPI. Its two interrupts can wake a host on motion or free fall, so the host can sleep the rest of the time.

Pin | Name | Type | Description
1 | VIN | Power | Supply, 2.4 to 5.5 V.
2 | GND | Ground | Ground.
3 | SCL | Input | I²C clock, or SPI clock. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
4 | SDA | I/O | I²C data, or SPI data in. Pull up to 3.3 V for I²C.
5 | SDO | Output | SPI data out. In I²C it sets the address: 0x68 low, 0x69 high.
6 | CS | Input | SPI chip select, active low. Held high on the board for I²C.
7 | INT1 | Output | Interrupt 1: data ready, or motion.
8 | INT2 | Output | Interrupt 2: free fall, or the FIFO full.
9 | FSYNC | Input | Frame sync from a camera. Tie to GND if unused.
10 | GND | Ground | Ground.

Table 1 Pin functions. Pin 1 is marked on the board by a triangle.
